title: SPHEREx 2025-2026 spectra confirm the warm excess of the old dipping star Gaia20cdd at 450-650 K; prior hot-silicate dust fails, and with WISE 12 um carbon grains at 2.5-4 au fit best
abstract: Gaia20cdd is a kinematically old K-type star with deep dust dips and a 4.6 um (WISE W2) excess. Prior campaign work fitted two one-population dust models to WISE W2 and W3: astrosilicate at 0.04-0.24 au and 940-1160 K, or graphite at 2.1-6.8 au and about 345 K. We used public SPHEREx quick-release images (477 exposures, 2025 June to 2026 July), forced PSF photometry with Gaia DR3 positions, and a photosphere template from 26 field stars of similar colour in the same images. SPHEREx detects the excess with a new instrument: epsilon = F/F_photosphere - 1 = 0.200 +- 0.028 at 3.83-5.00 um, larger than in all 26 controls. It increases from 0.03 +- 0.03 at 2.4-3.1 um to 0.29 +- 0.07 at 4.4-5.0 um, after we subtract a faint red source 5.6 arcsec away. The 16-arcsec bright neighbour shows no excess, and other template colours and normalisations give 0.22-0.31 at 4.4-5.0 um. One modified blackbody gives 477-651 K (beta = 2 to 0; 1 sigma range 411-808 K). The prior astrosilicate solutions give chi2 = 33-37 against 10.6 for the best fit, because they put too much excess at 2.5-3.8 um. The prior graphite solutions give chi2 = 18.5-19.5. With the AllWISE W3 excess added, graphite fits at 2.5-2.8 au (one star) or 3.7-4.1 au (K+K binary), and astrosilicate fits worse (delta chi2 about 1.5), because no single radius matches both SPHEREx and W3. The excess was constant in three visit windows. The star recovered from a shallow, colour-dependent dimming between 2025 Nov-Dec and 2026 May-Jul (+6.8 +- 1.5 percent at 0.75-1.09 um, +1.0 +- 1.3 percent at 1.6-2.4 um). The SPHEREx photosphere has BP-RP = 0.98, the quiet colour. The second dipper Gaia DR3 2870538750879109504 has no excess (-0.02 +- 0.03). The M dwarf Gaia DR3 3768075658908734720 has a tentative excess (0.18 +- 0.03; 8 controls). Limitations: early SPHEREx calibration, PSF fits with reduced chi2 about 2, a bright-star systematic offset of about 0.04, a template that can differ in metallicity, a low-significance W3 point, and one control star with a similar excess.
